_comment: Real Iowa (USDA zone 5) seasonal windows. First frost early-to-mid October, last frost early May. Angles must reference genuine deadlines only — never invented urgency.

lawn.1: Planning season. Next-season booking, early-bird scheduling, how sod and irrigation projects get budgeted.
lawn.2: Planning season. Irrigation system audits on paper, booking spring installs before the queue fills.
lawn.3: Irrigation startup and backflow testing. Assessing winter damage to turf and sprinkler lines.
lawn.4: Spring installs begin. Startup season, and booking before the spring queue fills up.
lawn.5: Peak sod install. New-construction lawns and first-season watering guidance.
lawn.6: Peak install season. Establishment care and watering schedules for new sod.
lawn.7: Heat stress and drought watering schedules. System efficiency and mid-season repairs.
lawn.8: Heat stress and mid-season repairs — and booking the September sod window now, before it fills.
lawn.9: The best sod window of the year: cool nights, warm soil. The strongest honest urgency of the season.
lawn.10: Winterization and sprinkler blowouts. Hard deadline before the first hard freeze.
lawn.11: Final blowouts and winterization. The freeze deadline is real and close.
lawn.12: Planning content, next-season booking, and how to budget a spring sod or irrigation project.

hardscape.1: Design and quoting season. Permit and engineering explainers, budgeting a spring build.
hardscape.2: Design and quoting season. Before-and-after archive, booking the spring build calendar.
hardscape.3: Post-thaw failure inspections: bulging walls, frost heave, spring runoff pooling.
hardscape.4: Post-thaw inspections and drainage failures. Booking the build season before it fills.
hardscape.5: Peak build season. Material education — block vs. boulder vs. timber vs. poured.
hardscape.6: Peak build season. Project showcases and what separates a wall that lasts from one that bulges.
hardscape.7: Peak build season. Drainage under heavy summer rain, erosion control.
hardscape.8: Peak build season, and the last stretch to book a build before the ground freezes.
hardscape.9: Last call before ground freeze. Drainage fixes ahead of winter.
hardscape.10: Ground-freeze deadline. Drainage and grading corrections before winter sets in.
hardscape.11: Design and quoting season. Permits, engineering, and planning a spring build.
hardscape.12: Design and quoting season. Before-and-after archive and spring project budgeting.

stumps.1: Winter grinding. Frozen ground means less lawn damage and easier equipment access.
stumps.2: Winter access advantages. Planning spring landscaping around stumps that need to go first.
stumps.3: Spring cleanup. Winter storm damage and clearing stumps before planting season.
stumps.4: Spring cleanup. Getting stumps out before sod, seeding, and landscaping season starts.
stumps.5: Clearing stumps ahead of summer projects. Root damage to lawns, mowers, and foundations.
stumps.6: Storm season. Downed trees, emergency removals, and what to do with what's left.
stumps.7: Storm season and raised roots. Trip hazards, mower damage, and post-storm cleanup.
stumps.8: Storm cleanup, and clearing stumps now so the ground is ready for the fall seeding window.
stumps.9: Clear stumps before fall seeding and sod. The best restoration window of the year.
stumps.10: Fall cleanup. Grinding before the ground freezes and restoration gets harder.
stumps.11: Last call before hard freeze. Planning winter access for what can wait.
stumps.12: Winter grinding. Frozen-ground advantages and planning spring landscape restoration.

roofing.1: Ice dams and winter leaks. Attic ventilation and insulation as the real cause.
roofing.2: Ice dams, snow load, and winter storm damage. What to check from the ground.
roofing.3: Spring inspections after winter. Wind damage, and booking before the spring rush.
roofing.4: Spring storm and hail season opens. Inspections and how insurance claims actually work.
roofing.5: Hail and wind season. Documenting storm damage and filing a claim without getting lowballed.
roofing.6: Peak storm season. Hail, wind, emergency repairs, and spotting damage from the ground.
roofing.7: Peak storm season. Heat, shingle aging, and why ventilation shortens or extends roof life.
roofing.8: Storm damage claims, and booking a replacement before the fall rush fills the calendar.
roofing.9: The fall replacement window. Booking before winter, and gutter prep ahead of the freeze.
roofing.10: The last good install window before winter. Gutters and ice-dam prevention.
roofing.11: Winter prep. Ice-dam prevention and being ready for an emergency repair.
roofing.12: Ice dams and winter leaks. Planning a spring replacement and budgeting for it.
